# Shared-baseline design

For a shared-baseline time-course with conditions $c = 1 \ldots C$, non-baseline
times $t = 1 \ldots T$, and a single shared baseline at time 0, the saturated
group-means design is:

$$X = \text{model.matrix}(\sim 0 + \text{group})$$

where the baseline is a **single** column shared by all conditions (not
replicated per condition). This avoids the inflation caused by copying the
baseline, which artificially weights day-0 in downstream clustering.

# Contrast families

`tps_make_contrasts()` builds six families:

- **vs-baseline**: $D_{c,t} = \mu_{c,t} - \mu_0$ (single t-tests)
- **within-condition**: consecutive or all-pairs temporal contrasts
- **average-time**: $A_t = \frac{1}{C}\sum_c \mu_{c,t} - \mu_0$ (omnibus F)
- **heterogeneity**: $\mu_{c,t} - \mu_{c_{ref},t}$ (omnibus F, full rank)
- **within-omnibus**: per-condition vs-baseline jointly (omnibus F)
- **endpoint**: $\mu_{c,t_{end}} - \mu_0$ (single t-tests)

## Note on reference-invariance

The heterogeneity family is reference-invariant in its **column subspace**:
changing the reference condition spans the same model-difference subspace
(equal rank). With complete feature-level observations, the resulting limma
F-tests agree up to floating-point tolerance. With missing values,
`limma::contrasts.fit()` uses an approximate covariance transformation, so
the numerical F-statistics can depend on the chosen reference even though the
tested subspace is identical. Report the selected reference and use a
sensitivity check when missingness is appreciable.

# Evidence-decomposed protein states

Rather than a black-box label, `tps_classify_states()` computes three
transparent axes:

1. **temporal_evidence**: from average-time + within-omnibus F-tests
2. **condition_heterogeneity**: from the heterogeneity F-test
3. **direction_pattern**: from endpoint contrast signs across conditions

These combine into a final `state`. Documented labels are
`stable_or_unresolved`, `shared_dynamic_up`, `shared_dynamic_down`,
`condition_dependent_dynamic`, `endpoint_up`, `endpoint_down`,
`temporal_only`, `heterogeneity_only`,
`cross_condition_opposite`, and `temporal_reversal`. The raw axes and
the rule manifest are always retained for auditability.

# Optional repeated measures

`tps_fit()` accepts `block` (a `colData` column name or a sample-aligned
vector) and optional `correlation`. When `block` is supplied and
`correlation` is `NULL`, the consensus correlation is estimated with
`limma::duplicateCorrelation()`. A column named `replicate` is never
treated as a block by default. The same `block` also selects the default
pathway significance engine (CAMERA without a block; ROMER with a block).

# Pathway NET / REM / COH summaries

For pathway $g$ and contrast $j$, with protein-level statistic $s_{i,j}$
(default: moderated t):

$$\text{NET}_{g,j} = \frac{\sum_i M_{g,i} s_{i,j}}{\sum_i M_{g,i}}, \quad
  \text{REM}_{g,j} = \frac{\sum_i M_{g,i} |s_{i,j}|}{\sum_i M_{g,i}}, \quad
  \text{COH}_{g,j} = \frac{|\text{NET}_{g,j}|}{\text{REM}_{g,j} + \varepsilon}$$

- **NET**: net directional shift
- **REM**: total remodeling magnitude
- **COH**: directional coherence in $[0,1]$

These quantities are **summaries**. They are not themselves a new
competitive gene-set test. COH has no p-value.

# Pathway significance: CAMERA and ROMER

Default calibration is `engine = "auto"` in `tps_calibrate_pathways()`
(ADR 0011):

- no `block` on the fit → `limma::camera` (independent arrays)
- `block` present → `limma::romer` (repeat-measures rotations)

Reported columns are `p_directional` / `q_directional` and
`p_mixed` / `q_mixed`. Explicit `engine = "camera"` aborts if the fit
has a block. `engine = "romer"` is allowed with or without a block.
`engine = "fry"` and `engine = "permutation"` are explicit only; auto
never switches engine because of missing values.

CAMERA is called with `sort = FALSE`, `inter.gene.cor = NA`, and
`trend.var` from the fit. Directional uses `directional = TRUE`
(parametric); mixed uses `directional = FALSE` and `use.ranks = TRUE`.
The package does not call `cameraPR`. Pathways are matched by name.

ROMER reports `P.Up`, `P.Down`, and `P.Mixed`. The package stores
`p_up` / `p_down`, sets `p_mixed = P.Mixed`, and defines
`p_directional = min(1, 2 * min(P.Up, P.Down))` (package convention).
Default rotations are `nrot = 9999`.

The competitive universe is formed once in
`tps_pathway_scores(tps_fit)`: features with finite statistics on the
selected family **and** complete expression on the inference samples.
Calibration does not change that universe or recompute NET/REM/COH.

This is not a claim of a new competitive test, and not a claim of
superiority versus CAMERA.

## Permutation+VIF diagnostic

Abundance-stratified label permutation with residual inter-gene VIF
(ADR 0005, 0010) remains available as `engine = "permutation"`. It is a
**diagnostic**, not the default significance engine. `vif_cap` is not
retuned (diagnostic default remains 3). Use it to inspect a
correlation-aware permutation null; do not treat it as a replacement
for CAMERA/ROMER in the default workflow.

# Contrast-driven pathway remodeling dynamics

The pathway scores (NET/REM/COH) are computed for each **contrast**. By
passing `family = "vs_baseline"` to `tps_pathway_scores()`, the package
obtains scores for every (condition, timepoint) pair — not just the
endpoint. This yields a **pathway remodeling trajectory**: how NET, REM,
and COH evolve over time, with per-timepoint CAMERA/ROMER significance.

`tps_classify_pathway_dynamics()` assigns **descriptive** trajectory
shape labels from per-time `q_directional` / `q_mixed`. The labels are
transparent rules, not class-specific statistical inferences:

- **early_directional**: first timepoint NET-significant with high COH
  and a persistent, directionally consistent NET signal
- **gradual_remodeling**: terminal REM is significant and more than 1.2-fold
  the first timepoint REM (no COH-rise requirement)
- **delayed_opposition**: the final supported NET direction reverses an earlier
  supported direction
- **transient_burst**: REM peaks mid-course, then subsides
- **directional_delayed**: NET becomes significant at later timepoints
  (or is significant but does not meet the early-directional rule)
- **sustained_remodeling**: at least one timepoint has significant REM
  and no timepoint has significant NET

Cross-condition **divergence** is reported as a separate flag at a matched
timepoint when two significant NET directions oppose one another, or when a
significant direction opposes a non-significant NET with magnitude above 0.1.

`tps_calibrate_dynamics()` supplies a trajectory-level p-value that is
**independent of the shape label**. For each pathway × condition it takes
the Bonferroni-minP of the time-point directional and mixed p-values;
`q_dynamic` is one global BH over pathway × condition. `q_dynamic` is not
a class test of `dynamic_state`, and it is not a permutation test.

The full rank-audited contrast family's moderated statistics drive the
pathway summaries, preserving direction and uncertainty at every timepoint.
`tps_link_states_pathways()` further connects
protein-level evidence states to pathway-level dynamics when protein
identifiers are mapped onto the pathway gene space (pass a **named**
`protein_ids` vector keyed by `feature_id` when `term2gene$gene` is a
locus tag rather than the fit row name).

# Correlated-pathway simulation

`tps_simulate_correlated_pathways()` generates a shared-baseline
experiment with an explicit disjoint pathway membership and
compound-symmetric within-pathway correlation
`epsilon[i in k] = sqrt(rho)*Z_k + sqrt(1-rho)*E_i`.
`within_pathway_cor = 0` is independent noise;
`pathway_signal` is `"none"`, `"codirectional"`, or `"mixed"`.
The object includes `term2gene` for `tps_pathway_scores()`.

The simulator is a known-truth check for summaries and engine behavior.
It is not used to claim type-I or power superiority versus CAMERA.

# Related software

- **CAMERA** (limma): competitive gene-set testing with an inter-gene
  correlation adjustment; the default significance engine here when
  arrays are independent (no `block`).
- **ROMER** (limma): rotation-based competitive gene-set testing in
  linear models; the default significance engine here when a
  repeat-measures `block` is set.
- **fry** (limma): a fast self-contained rotation gene-set test (a fast
  approximation to ROAST); available as an explicit engine, never
  selected by `engine = "auto"`.
- **piano**: consensus gene-set analysis that reports distinct-up,
  distinct-down, and mixed directional hypotheses.
- **directPA**: direction-specific perturbation analysis for proteomics
  pathway responses.
- **TcGSA**: time-course gene-set analysis for self-contained
  longitudinal gene-set effects.
